title: P's and Q's
label: 679 Recordings

sound.text: PopMatters (2005) hears a heavily synthesised backbeat darting between the stereo channels over an imposing, hypnotic bass line, and calls it the most kinetic track on Run the Road.
Stereogum (2016) describes a frantic beat that Kano rides 'effortlessly', and calls it a model for how grime should sound.
Fiddy describes the 679 remix featuring Lethal B, Ghetto and Demon as 'As good as the original, just crunk it.'

context.text: Kano's debut single on the independent label 679. RBMA calls it an underground anthem that marked him as a rising star.
Already playlisted on Choice FM by early November 2004, according to Fiddy.
Certified Gold in May 2025, mainly on streaming and downloads.
A contemporary dissent: Vice's Grimewatch (Nov 2004) called it a 'soft single' and 'far from his best work'.

rels.other: P's & Q's (remix) feat. Lethal B, Ghetto and Demon (679, 2004)

uncertainty: The format and catalogue number of the first release are not verified, because Discogs (which lists release IDs 350982 and 324366 and master 167599) could not be fetched. Stereogum dates the track 2005, while Wikipedia and RBMA give 2004 (November 2004 per Wikipedia). No chart position was verified. Wikipedia says 'Typical Me' was Kano's first UK Singles Chart appearance, which implies P's and Q's did not chart, but this is an inference.
tracklist: Written by K. Robinson and C. Chichester (45worlds credits). Also appears on Run the Road (Jan 2005), as the B-side of the 'Typical Me' CD single (679L096CD1), and as track 3 of Home Sweet Home (2005). Fiddy (Nov 2004) reports a 679 remix with verses from Lethal B, Ghetto and Demon.
